threats.name: Use After Free
threats.rationale: Use after free needs manual deallocation. GHC-compiled Haskell reclaims heap values with a garbage collector only when unreachable, so a live reference never dangles. The residual routes are the FFI (foreign import, Foreign.Ptr, ForeignPtr finalizers), unsafePerformIO-wrapped allocation and primops, none of which the library uses; Safe Haskell, once the module carries the pragma, makes GHC itself reject them.

threats.name: NULL Pointer Dereference
threats.rationale: Haskell has no null. Its analogue is a Maybe that is forced with fromJust, a pattern match that does not cover Nothing, or undefined: each raises an exception when evaluated. The library returns Maybe in one place (triState, Combinational.hs:120-124, Nothing meaning high impedance) and consumes none. Closed by the partial-function analyzer rule plus -Wincomplete-patterns with -Werror, neither of which is live.

closed_by.detail: No use of head, tail, init, last, (!!), fromJust, fromRight/fromLeft partial uses, read, toEnum, succ/pred, foldr1/foldl1, maximum/minimum on a possibly empty list, error, errorWithoutStackTrace, undefined, `throw`, `assert`, div/mod/quot/rem with a divisor that is not provably nonzero, (^) with an exponent that is not provably non-negative ((^) throws on a negative exponent), and no function whose pattern match is not exhaustive. threats.name: Integer Overflow to Buffer Boundary
threats.rationale: The narrow registry class: an Int that wraps and then sizes or indexes a buffer. Haskell Int arithmetic wraps silently (no exception). The only sizes the library derives from caller data are `2 ^ length sel` and `2 ^ length inputs` (Combinational.hs:73,87,95): `2 ^ 64` is 0 in an Int, which is why a cap of 16 select bits is checked BEFORE any exponentiation (:54-58, :68, :84, :93) and tested at 17, 63, 64 and 65 (LogicGatesSpec.hs:158-167). The general class is haskell.silent-int-wraparound; this row is only about wraparound reaching a size.

closed_by.detail: LG02 section 9 for a statically typed lane: only the wide-integer rows can be written. Present: -1, 2, 255, 256, 257 and every Int in [-1024, 1024] (test/LogicGatesSpec.hs:54-62), minBound, minBound+1, maxBound-1, maxBound. ABSENT as explicit rows: 2^31, 2^32, 2^32+1, 2^53+1 (outside the sweep), so a gate that kept only the low 8, 16 or 32 bits of an Int would not be caught by anything except the extremes. String, float, Bool, Maybe and list rows cannot be written: GHC refuses them (the signatures are monomorphic Int).

Planned: run the suite under at least two GHC versions (the CI pin 9.4.8 plus a current one) so Int width, defaulting and warning behaviour are not tested under a single compiler. CI installs only GHC 9.4.8 with Cabal 3.10.3.0 (ci.yml jobs `unicode17-haskell-conformance` and `build`, haskell-actions/setup pins bda9c52 and 6037f33); no second implementation is exercised.

threats.name: A gate returns before validating both arguments (Incorrect Short Circuit Evaluation)
threats.rationale: Haskell's `&&`, `||` and the Either monad short-circuit. A gate written as `if a == 0 then Right 0 else ...` would accept AND 0 2. Every basic gate here validates every parameter through the Either monad before the result expression, so AND 0 2 is rejected, and the NAND-built gates validate up front (Basic.hs:100-104, 191-252). The LG02 section 9 short-circuit rows (decisive first argument with an invalid second, and the reverse) are the sweep with the other argument 0 and 1 (LogicGatesSpec.hs:96-101).

closed_by.detail: test/LogicGatesSpec.hs (hspec, run by `cabal test`, BUILD:3): literal truth tables for 9 binary and 2 unary gates, NAND-built included (:35-52, written as literals, never computed by the code under test); NAND-built equals direct (:81-89); every Int in [-1024, 1024] other than 0 and 1, plus minBound, minBound+1, maxBound-1, maxBound (2,051 distinct invalid values, :59-62) in each argument position with the other argument 0 and 1, asserting the structural `InvalidBit "a"|"b" value` (:91-101); first-invalid-parameter reporting when both are bad (:100-101); no inner NAND wire name leaks (:103-113); valid input never fails (:126-130). NOT covered: the suite never calls encoder, priorityEncoder, triState or mux4 and reaches srLatch only through dLatch; bad-bit rejection of demux, decoder, encoder, priorityEncoder, triState, mux4, mux8 and the sequential blocks beyond one example each (dLatch d and e, dFlipFlop clock, mux2 sel: :115-124); no property test; no hpc coverage run (BUILD:3 is plain `cabal test`).

threats.name: Reliance on an insufficiently trustworthy build component (Hackage and Cabal supply chain; also CWE-494)
threats.rationale: The published library has no dependency but base (logic-gates.cabal:15), a boot library that ships with GHC. The test suite pulls hspec == 2.* and its tree from Hackage with no freeze file, no index-state and no hash (code/packages/haskell/cabal.project is `packages: */` and `tests: True`), the bound `base >= 4.7 && < 5` admits compilers a decade older than the CI pin, Hackage revisions can change a package's dependency bounds after release, and the toolchain is whatever haskell-actions/setup installs (GHC 9.4.8, Cabal 3.10.3.0, ci.yml haskell-actions/setup steps). A compromised test dependency runs code on the build machine.

considered_not_included.name: Improper Validation of Array Index
considered_not_included.why_not: No array and no `!!`: the library never indexes a caller list by a caller number (Combinational.hs:88-89, 96-97 compare a counter with a computed index). Folded into CWE-20 and haskell.cwe-125.

considered_not_included.name: Use of Externally-Controlled Format String
considered_not_included.why_not: No printf or Text.Printf import; Haskell's printf format is checked by type class and the library does not use it.

considered_not_included.name: Off-by-one Error
considered_not_included.why_not: Folded into haskell.cwe-20 and haskell.unbounded-lazy-list-input: the boundary cases (16 accepted, 17 rejected; cap and cap+1 widths) are the cap tests (LogicGatesSpec.hs:158-182).

considered_not_included.name: Unchecked Return Value
considered_not_included.why_not: The result is an Either: a caller cannot obtain the Bit without unwrapping it, so the Left cannot be silently ignored the way a C status code can; a caller can still default it with `either (const 1) id`, which the package cannot prevent. Not a package weakness.

considered_not_included.name: Divide By Zero
considered_not_included.why_not: div and mod use a literal 2 divisor (Combinational.hs:131; Sequential.hs:141) or the computed `2 ^ bit` (Combinational.hs:106,117), which is nonzero for 0 <= bit <= 62. `2 ^ bit` would be 0 only for bit at least 64, which needs a list longer than 2^63. Folded into haskell.partial-functions-and-bottoms (the planned analyzer rule requires a provably nonzero divisor and a provably non-negative exponent).

considered_not_included.name: Declaration of Catch for Generic Exception
considered_not_included.why_not: The library catches nothing (no catch, handle, try or bracket).

considered_not_included.name: Declaration of Throws for Generic Exception
considered_not_included.why_not: The library throws nothing; it returns Either (Basic.hs:17-26).

considered_not_included.name: Missing Release of Memory after Effective Lifetime
considered_not_included.why_not: Garbage collected. A lazy result can retain its inputs until forced (the Right of demux holds the sel list, at most 16 elements, until the index is evaluated); bounded by the caps and folded into haskell.unbounded-lazy-list-input.

considered_not_included.name: Use of Uninitialized Variable
considered_not_included.why_not: Haskell bindings are initialised where they are defined and immutable; there is no uninitialised read, only `undefined`, covered by haskell.partial-functions-and-bottoms.

considered_not_included.name: Use of Externally-Controlled Input to Select Classes or Code (Unsafe Reflection)
considered_not_included.why_not: No Typeable cast, Dynamic, Data, Generics or Template Haskell in the library; folded into haskell.cwe-94 and haskell.cwe-843 through analyzer-rule:haskell.no-eval-reflection-dynamic-loading.

considered_not_included.name: Use of Incorrect Operator
considered_not_included.why_not: Gate bodies are single comparisons and conditionals (`a' == 1 && b' == 1`, Basic.hs:104,118,132); the literal truth tables in the suite (LogicGatesSpec.hs:35-52) would catch a wrong operator. Functional correctness is the Warrant and truth-table evidence, not a registry class.

considered_not_included.name: Dead Code
considered_not_included.why_not: The `_ -> Left` arm of mux4 after `length sel /= 2` is unreachable (Combinational.hs:28,39). It is deliberate: it keeps the case total under -Wincomplete-patterns. Benign, not a weakness.

considered_not_included.name: Function Call with Incorrectly Specified Arguments
considered_not_included.why_not: Same-typed positional arguments (dFlipFlop takes six Ints, Sequential.hs:70) can be swapped by a caller undetected; an ergonomics risk that produces a wrong answer, not a registry-class weakness. A newtype per role would remove it and is an API change outside this list.

considered_not_included.name: Incorrect Conversion between Numeric Types
considered_not_included.why_not: The library converts nothing (no fromIntegral, toEnum or realToFrac); folded into haskell.cwe-704 and haskell.caller-side-fromintegral-truncation.

considered_not_included.name: Incorrect Calculation
